1/4: The thing about digital products is they come wrapped in guarantees and refund windows that feel solid until you actually need them. You read the terms once, click agree, and assume you know what you bought. Spoiler: the refund conditions, billing cycles, and guarantee periods shift depending on which offer you grabbed. 2/4: I spent twenty years marketing online. I've built systems, sold digital products, watched creators struggle with their own checkout flows. What I know now is that cancelling cleanly requires you to know three things first: when your guarantee actually expires, what "refund window" really means for your specific purchase, and whether your plan grandfathered you into different terms than what's listed today. These aren't footnotes. They're the difference between getting your money back and being stuck.

3/4: The refund isn't guaranteed just because you're unhappy. It's guaranteed if you act within the window they specify for the offer you bought. The subscription doesn't auto-refund when you cancel. You cancel the recurring charge and then follow the actual refund request process. These are two separate things and I've watched people miss refunds because they thought cancellation was enough.

4/4: Before you reach out to support or assume you're locked in, pull up your original receipt and confirmation email. Look at the date. Look at what offer name appears. These aren't footnotes. They're the difference between getting your money back and being stuck.

3/4: The refund isn't guaranteed just because you're unhappy. It's guaranteed if you act within the window they specify for the offer you bought. The subscription doesn't auto-refund when you cancel. You cancel the recurring charge and then follow the actual refund request process. These are two separate things and I've watched people miss refunds because they thought cancellation was enough.

4/4: Before you reach out to support or assume you're locked in, pull up your original receipt and confirmation email. Look at the date. Look at what offer name appears. That determines your window, your refund conditions, and what you're entitled to. It's boring work. It's also the only work that actually protects you.

captions.threads:
